A SLIDE BOOK · 14 LECTURES
Harness Engineering
Why strong AI coding agents still fail, and the engineering around the model that makes Claude Code and Codex reliable.
Harness Engineering · Welcome · 01
WELCOME · THE CORE IDEA
A harness builds a working system around the model
It doesn't make the model smarter. It closes the loop: the agent acts, the harness checks, feedback goes back until the work is really done.

Harness Engineering · L01 · 05
WHERE AGENTS ACTUALLY GET STUCK
Agents get stuck in five places
Each failure maps to one harness layer, and each layer is something you can fix.
Diagram
Vague task
“Add search”: full-text? paginated? It has to guess.
Unwritten rules
The SQLAlchemy 2.0 rule lives only in Slack.
Broken setup
Context burns on pip errors and Node versions.
No checks
With no tests, it's done when it feels done.
Lost memory
Each new session re-explores from zero.
Task spec
Context
Environment
Verification
State
Rule: when it fails, don't swap the model first. Name the layer that broke and fix that.
Harness Engineering · L01 · 06
THE DIAGNOSTIC LOOP
When it fails, fix the harness first
Treat each failure as a signal about one layer. Fix that layer, and the agent stops failing that way.
Flow
1 · Run
Give the agent the task
2 · Observe
See exactly what failed
3 · Attribute
Which of the five layers?
4 · Fix
Repair that one layer
5 · Re-run
Confirm it's gone
repeat until the harness stops failing in that way
TINY FAILURE LOG

Fix pagination bug
Pass

Harness Engineering · L01 · 07
DEFINITION OF DONE
Write a Definition of Done for every task
Without one, the agent invents its own. Make done something a command can check.
How to
What people type
“Add a search feature.”
The agent must guess: search what, how many results, highlighted or not, which tests?
task.md
Completion criteria: - New endpoint GET /api/search?q=xxx - Pagination, default 20 items - Results include highlighted snippets - All new code passes pytest - mypy --strict passes
First step: add AGENTS.md at the repo root with the stack, the conventions and the exact verify commands.

Harness Engineering · L01 · 10
LECTURE 02
What a harness actually is
A prompt file is not a harness. A harness is five subsystems: instructions, tools, environment, state and feedback.
Harness Engineering · L02 · 11
THE FIVE-SUBSYSTEM MODEL
Five subsystems wrap the agent
Rules and state flow in, tools act on a runtime, and check results flow back to the agent.
Animated diagram
Harness Engineering · L02 · 12
WHAT GOES IN EACH SUBSYSTEM
Each subsystem has one clear job
Use this as an audit list: score each one from 1 to 5 and fix the lowest first.
How to
Instructions
AGENTS.md: overview, stack + versions, first-run commands, hard rules, doc links
Tools
Shell, files, tests. Least privilege, but never so tight it can't install deps
Environment
Locked deps, pinned versions (.nvmrc), Docker or devcontainer
State
PROGRESS.md: done, in progress, blocked. Read at start, update at end
Feedback
Verify commands listed in AGENTS.md. Highest return per hour
Harness Engineering · L02 · 13
HARNESSES YOU ALREADY USE
The tools you know are harnesses too
Each one has the same five parts. Their weak spots show up exactly where a subsystem is missing.
Comparison
Tool
Rules file
What it does well
Where it breaks
Claude Code
CLAUDE.md
Shell, local env, session history, runs tests
Can't verify if you never say how to test
Cursor
.cursorrules
Terminal, reads project and lint config
Weak state: reopen the IDE, context is gone
Codex
AGENTS.md
Worktree per task, local logs and traces
Much weaker in a bare repo
AutoGPT
—
Long autonomous runs
No state, no precise feedback: it loops
Harness Engineering · L02 · 14
WHERE TO START
Start with feedback: cheapest, highest return
Write the verify commands down. Then measure which subsystem matters most by removing one at a time.
How to
AGENTS.md
Verification commands: - Tests: pytest tests/ -x - Type check: mypy src/ --strict - Lint: ruff check src/ - Full: make check
Ablation test
Keep the model fixed.
Remove one subsystem at a time.
The biggest drop is the most valuable part today.
Remember: harness rots like code. Audit it on a schedule and pay down harness debt like tech debt.

Knowledge outside the repo is invisible

Harness Engineering · L03 · 18
THE FRESH-SESSION TEST
Five questions a new session must answer
Open a brand-new session with only the repo. Every question it can't answer is a blank spot on your map.
How to
What is this system?
AGENTS.md / README
How is it organized?
ARCHITECTURE.md / module docs
How do I run it?
Makefile / init.sh / package scripts
How do I verify it?
test, lint and check commands
Where are we now?
PROGRESS.md / feature list / git log
Harness Engineering · L03 · 19
DRAWING A GOOD MAP
Four rules for an agent-readable repo
Put knowledge next to the code it governs, keep it short but complete, and change it in the same commit.
How to
1
Next to the code — a short doc in each module folder
2
One entry file — AGENTS.md, 50–100 lines
3
Minimal, complete — every rule earns its place
4
Update together — doc changes ride in the same commit
repo layout
project/ ├── AGENTS.md # entry ├── src/ │ ├── api/ │ │ └── ARCHITECTURE.md │ └── db/ │ └── CONSTRAINTS.md ├── PROGRESS.md # progress └── Makefile # setup, test
Harness Engineering · L03 · 20
STATE MANAGEMENT
Treat agent state like a database: ACID
A borrowed idea from database transactions that turns “keep the repo sane” into four checks.
Concept
A · Atomicity
All or nothing. Commit only when the change is complete and verified.
C · Consistency
After every step, tests pass and lint is clean.
I · Isolation
Parallel agents get their own branch or progress file.
D · Durability
What must survive lives in git-tracked files.
Watch out: out-of-date docs are worse than none. They lead the agent the wrong way while it feels sure it's right.
Harness Engineering · L03 · 21
REAL-LIFE SCENARIO
Example: the rule that lived in Slack
A typical story (illustrative). The fix is the right note in the right place, not more documents.
Example
Slack
“All APIs need OAuth 2.0”
Agent
Adds /export endpoint
Result
No auth: it never saw the rule
Fix
Add it to ARCHITECTURE.md in src/api
Next session
Follows the rule
Exercise: list your project's key decisions and mark each “in repo” or “outside”. Aim for under 10% outside.

THE VICIOUS CYCLE
The “just add a rule” trap
Each mistake adds a rule. It helps for a while, then the file bloats and the agent does worse.

Harness Engineering · L04 · 24
WHAT GOES WRONG
Five ways a giant file hurts
More rules don't add up to more compliance. They compete for the same attention.
Concept
Context eaten
600 lines ≈ 10–20K tokens, 8–15% of a 128K window
Lost in the middle
Rules buried mid-file get used least
Priority blur
“Never use eval()” looks like “prefer functional style”
Maintenance decay
Adding feels free, deleting feels risky. It only grows
Contradictions
“Strict TypeScript” vs “legacy files may use any”
Low signal
A bug fix reads 50 lines of deploy notes
Harness Engineering · L04 · 25
LOST IN THE MIDDLE
Rules in the middle get missed
Models recall the start and end of long text best. A security rule at line 300 of 600 sits in the blind spot.
Animated diagram
Where to put a must-follow rule
Top or bottom of the entry file, never the middle.
Better: a topic doc loaded only when the task needs it.
Harness Engineering · L04 · 26
HOW TO SPLIT
Make AGENTS.md a router, not an encyclopedia
Keep what's always needed at hand, tuck away what's sometimes needed, and drop what's never needed.
How to
AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md Python 3.11 FastAPI · PostgreSQL 15 ## Quick start make setup · make test · make check ## Hard constraints - OAuth 2.0 on every API - SQLAlchemy 2.0 syntax only ## Topic docs - docs/api-patterns.md (new endpoints) - docs/database-rules.md (DB changes)
Entry file
50–200 lines: overview, run commands, ≤15 hard rules, links
Topic docs
50–150 lines each, read only when the task needs them
Every rule notes
Why it was added · when it applies · when it can go
Harness Engineering · L04 · 27
WHAT THE EVIDENCE SAYS
Shorter helps efficiency, not magic accuracy
Three sources the course cites. Read them as “test your instructions”, not “shorter always wins”.
Evidence
OpenAI
Moved to a ~100-line entry file plus a docs folder kept fresh by linters and CI
ETH Zurich
Context files didn't generally raise success and cost 20%+ more. Keep rules minimal
Lulla et al.
With AGENTS.md: median runtime −28.64%, output tokens −16.58%
Takeaway: measure. Run the same 5 tasks before and after a split and compare.

LECTURE 05
Why long-running tasks lose continuity
Context windows are finite. Treat the agent like an engineer whose short-term memory is wiped every session.
Harness Engineering · L05 · 29
SESSION CONTINUITY
Every new session starts with amnesia
Without handoff files the next session rediscovers everything. With them, it rebuilds in minutes.
Diagram
WITHOUT HANDOFF FILES
Session 1
Feature half done
Context full
Session ends
Session 2
Starts from zero
Guessing
Repeats work, drifts
WITH HANDOFF FILES
PROGRESS.md
Done · doing · next
DECISIONS.md
Why A, not B
Verify notes
What passes, what fails
Git checkpoint
Exact repo state
Session 2
Picks up fast
Harness Engineering · L05 · 30
COMPACTION VS RESET
Compaction keeps the “what” and loses the “why”
Summaries keep the code's story but drop the reasoning. A reset starts clean but needs good handoff files.
Concept
Compaction: summarize in place
Keeps continuity in one session
Often loses why a choice was made
Context anxiety stays: it still rushes
Reset: new session from files
Clean head, no “running out” rush
Only as good as the handoff files
Needs progress + decision notes
Model matters: Sonnet 4.5 needed resets; Opus 4.5 managed with compaction. Design for the model you actually run.
Harness Engineering · L05 · 31
THE HANDOFF FILES
Write down what, why and what's next
A progress file tells the next session where things stand. A decision log tells it why.
How to
PROGRESS.md
## Current state Commit abc1234 · tests 42/43 · lint ok ## Done [x] User model + migration [x] CRUD endpoints ## In progress [ ] Pagination (edge-case test fails) ## Next 1. Fix pagination edge case
DECISIONS.md
## 2024-01-15 Redis for prefs cache Why: read every call Rejected: PG view Rule: TTL 5 min
Harness Engineering · L05 · 32
CLOCK IN, CLOCK OUT
A shift routine for every session
Put these two routines in AGENTS.md so every session starts and ends the same way.
How to
Clock in
1. Read PROGRESS.md
2. Read DECISIONS.md
3. Run make check
4. Continue from “Next”
Clock out
1. Update PROGRESS.md
2. Run make check
3. Commit finished work
15 → 3 min
rebuild time a good harness aims for
Rule: past ~60% of the window, prepare the handoff.

WHAT OVERREACH LOOKS LIKE
Ask for registration, get six half-done jobs

Harness Engineering · L07 · 41
ATTENTION IS A BUDGET
Split attention k ways and each task gets C/k
When C/k falls below what one task needs, nothing finishes. That's arithmetic, not a metaphor.

completion with a “small next step” strategy (Anthropic)

Why feature lists are harness primitives

Harness Engineering · L08 · 45
WHAT DOES “DONE” MEAN?
A memo can't tell the next session anything
“Mostly done” is not a state. The next session can't act on it, so it guesses or redoes work.
Concept
The note
“Did user auth, shopping cart mostly done, still need payments”
Questions nobody can answer
What does “mostly done” mean?
Which cart tests passed?
What's blocking payments?
20 min
spent inferring state, sometimes redoing features
−60–80%
startup diagnosis time with good progress records

THE TRIPLE
Every feature row needs three fields

The exact command to run
State
not_started · active · blocked · passing

LOOP VS GRAPH
A loop defers decisions; a graph makes them up front
Loops forgive vague design. Graphs make you admit how much of your workflow isn't modeled yet.
Comparison
Loop: deferred decision
One agent takes on everything
Cheap to start, failures invisible
Best for exploration
Graph: up-front decision
Who owns what, where failures go
Readable, auditable, repairable
Best for production
In short: a loop hides the problem inside the loop; a graph puts it on paper.

Goodhart
Ticket-closure rate rose; churn doubled. The bot learned to close tickets
Blind upward

Speed loop vs quality loop: each dashboard green, system thrashing

Harness Engineering · L14 · 93
GRAPH VS WORKFLOW
A graph is a workflow whose nodes can think
Same skeleton as Airflow or Temporal. The new part: a node can be a whole agent.
Concept
Workflow node
Deterministic code: run tests, compute coverage
Agent node

Human node
Approval: the graph pauses until you nod
Who decides control flow? Your code → workflow. The model at runtime → agent. A graph can contain both.
